cues: Why do potassium and silver salts give different products?
Cyanide and nitrite can attack through two different atoms.
Potassium cyanide is ionic: the free cyanide ion attacks through carbon, the atom carrying the charge, giving a nitrile.
Silver cyanide is largely covalent: the carbon is tied up in the bond to silver, so attack must come through nitrogen, giving an isocyanide.
Nitrite is just the same: potassium nitrite attacks through oxygen, silver nitrite through nitrogen.
This is asked every single year.
